## A good historical average can hide a bad current return

Switch the decision window from all 156 weeks to the last quarter. The green bars show each channel's **true sales return on ad spend** in the workshop's seeded data; the orange bars are the break-even return for your assumed gross margin. The 3D view shows how a time window changes the data a model must explain. The lab fits static and time-varying Bayesian marketing mix models and reports 94% highest-density intervals around their estimates.

**Work one example.** At 30% margin, $1 of media needs $3.33 of sales to pay back. Social returns $4.00 per dollar over all three years and $2.11 in the last quarter. The recent window argues for cutting or testing before renewing; the all-period average argues for keeping. The [module](../modules/17-mmm-time-varying.qmd) quantifies uncertainty and gives a decision rule based on posterior probability.

**Data.** [Seeded synthetic weekly media series](https://github.com/project-delphi/ml-for-growth-marketing/blob/main/data/synthetic/mmm_drift_weekly.csv) and [generator truth](https://github.com/project-delphi/ml-for-growth-marketing/blob/main/data/synthetic/truth_mmm_drift.json). The all-period and last-quarter return values come from the truth file; gross margin is your scenario input.
